title: First derived inverse limit vanishes for eventually invertible towers
statement: Let $(A_n,f_n:A_{n+1}\to A_n)_{n\ge0}$ be an inverse system of abelian groups [def-weil-inverse-system]. Suppose there is $m\ge0$ such that $f_n$ is an isomorphism for every $n\ge m$. Then $R^1\varprojlim_n A_n=0$, where $R^1\varprojlim$ is the first right derived functor of the additive inverse-limit functor [def-sp-left-exact-additive].

source.place: Tag 07KW (lemma-Rlim), part (3), specialized to eventually constant systems; Tag 08D4 (perfect.tex, lemma-application-nice-K-injective), proof of (2)

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-derived-limit-roos-abelian-groups] to identify the first right derived inverse limit with the cokernel of the transition endomorphism 1-s [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism].

Write P for the product with projections pr_n. Choose m after which each f_n is invertible. Define maps q_n:P→A_n starting with q_m=0. Recursively upwards put q_(n+1)=(q_n-pr_n) followed by f_n inverse. Recursively downwards below m put q_n=pr_n+q_(n+1) followed by f_n. The two recursions give q_n-q_(n+1) followed by f_n=pr_n at every n, including m=0. Product extensionality shows that the product lift of the q_n followed by 1-s is the identity. Thus 1-s is a split epimorphism, its cokernel is zero, and the Roos isomorphism transports this zero object to R^1 lim A.
